citation.author: Tuominen, Juho
citation.title: Rockstar's Open World Video Games as Ideological Apparatuses: A Case Study of Red Dead Redemption Series

discipline: game studies / media studies (Marxist-Althusserian cultural critique); Tampere University, Internet and Game Studies
thesis: Rockstar's single-player open-world games function as ideological apparatuses on two levels: as nodes of the wider cultural ISA, and as self-contained worlds that internally simulate their own RSA and ISAs which 'hail' and interpellate the player to progress and thereby absorb the game's ideology; read as a whole (RDR2 + RDR), the series is 'mainstream but radically progressive,' transplanting the radical Italian (Spaghetti) Western's RSA-plot to unmask the neoliberal-capitalist state rather than endorse it.
sections: 1 Introduction (politics of virtual worlds; three reasons for Althusserian reading; case scope RDR+RDR2 single-player)

2 Theoretical Framework (2.1 Althusser/ISA, open-world genre, radical Italian Western; 2.2 video-game literacy; 2.3 games as rhetorical tools; 2.4 open world as experience; 2.5 politics of the open world)
3 Literature Review (3.1 Althusser and video games; 3.2 other studies of Rockstar/RDR)
4 Methodology (4.1 formal + critical analysis; close reading; reflexivity; played each game twice)
5 Analysis (5.1 Rockstar context/method; 5.2 game overview, rules/gameplay, formal+critical close reading; 5.3 RDR as ideological apparatus)
7 Conclusions (+7.1 future research: GTA+RDR timeline, Finnish games)
concepts: Ideological State Apparatus (ISA) and Repressive State Apparatus (RSA) - located both in culture and inside the diegesis
Interpellation / hailing - game hails the player to submit and to progress; progression = ideological absorption
Two-level apparatus / open-world ideology (game as cultural ISA AND world rendering its own apparatuses) (after Quijano-Cruz)
Directed / illusory freedom; 'experiences of experiences'; every choice already made (Mitchell, Muriel & Crawford, Zizek)
Radical Italian (Spaghetti) Western and its four plot variants, esp. the Repressive State Apparatus plot (Fisher 2014)
Player-as-revolutionary: mastering a game = capturing State power; designer:player :: ruling class:proletariat
Woke gaming (Gray & Leonard 2018) - Jack Marston as surviving alternative
Field of possibilities / incomplete universe: what is rendered possible vs. impossible encodes a worldview
Series-as-canon: ideology legible only across RDR2+RDR analyzed chronologically
readings: RDR/RDR2 simulate Althusser's apparatuses internally: Pinkertons/US Army/lawmen as RSA; gang cast, side activities, in-world institutions as ISAs
Read the series as one whole (RDR2 rise then RDR fall) to make its ideology legible
RDR2 = 'Long live the alternative': keeps a multicultural quasi-socialist utopia alive; pushes progressive values (anti-racism, women's suffrage); collective stash read as socialist
RDR = 'Outlaws to the end' / mourning the lost alternative; John Marston is an OUTLAW not a cowboy; reluctant revolutionary refusing 'the only option of neoliberalism'
State's betrayal of John (extort then murder despite freedom deal) exposes its coercive RSA nature
Jack Marston as the 'woke,' educated youth carrying the surviving revolutionary hope
The Rockstar contradiction: progressive/communal game content vs. the studio's crunch, fear-management, exploitation, ~8yr/2000-staff, ~$1B production
GTA+RDR combined timeline: RDR lays foundations, GTA simulates the resulting hypercapitalist 'theme park' America; RDR2 reads as opposing Trump/alt-right by valorizing community

game_elements.element: Honor system (good/bad acts move heroic<->unheroic scale; affects pay, merchant/black-market discounts, NPC reactions)
game_elements.how_treated: Read as ideologically incoherent yet ideology-bearing: player must commit dishonorable acts (beating hostages in train robberies) to advance 'heroic'; the mechanic carries direct content.

game_elements.element: Killing Ku Klux Klan members costs no honor
game_elements.how_treated: The rules thereby 'imply that killing racists is okay' - clearest case of a mechanic reinforcing a progressive ideology directly.

game_elements.element: Collective stash / donations + 'check the books' ledger
game_elements.how_treated: Read as socialist redistribution; ledger reveals Arthur as most generous contributor (seeds disillusionment); gang stays 'chronically poor' so in-game money is narratively near-irrelevant.

game_elements.element: Main-mission vs. side-activity economy (main missions = largest rewards, mostly crime; side quests/fishing/hunting/gambling/chores = small/entertainment)
game_elements.how_treated: Side content 'exists solely to interpellate a player to progress'; reward gradient hails the player toward the linear story.

game_elements.element: Van der Linde NPC cast + side quests as the game's ISAs
game_elements.how_treated: Cast and activities explicitly identified as in-game ISAs that hail the player to invest, regardless of real-world resemblance.

game_elements.element: Dutch's 'Tahiti' utopia plan / 'we rob Uncle Sam and leave'
game_elements.how_treated: A Robin Hood facade masking personal gain; the false promise that engineers the player's interpellation toward continued crime.

game_elements.element: Bank-manager line: 'Congratulations! You are now a real American, indebted and owned by the bank!'
game_elements.how_treated: Read as the game congratulating the player's submission to the neoliberal state when John takes a ranch loan.

game_elements.element: 'You can season meat with herbs but cannot swim underwater' boundary
game_elements.how_treated: Emblem of the designed 'incomplete universe': possible-vs-impossible always encodes a worldview.

game_elements.element: Slogans 'Outlaws for Life' (RDR2) vs. 'Outlaws to the End' (RDR)
game_elements.how_treated: Read as encoding the series arc from living alternative (hope) to its inevitable loss (fatalism).

game_elements.element: Story-completion statistic (~22% of PS4 players finished RDR2 by Jan 2019)
game_elements.how_treated: Used to argue experiences diverge by approach; 'cowboy-simulator' play = a failure of interpellation (game won't reward it as progress).

game_elements.element: Spaghetti-Western set-piece borrowings (Fort Mercer assault ~ Django; 'Tall Trees' ~ Il Grande Silenzio; revolutionary Mexico ~ Per un pugno di dollari)
game_elements.how_treated: Formal evidence that RDR transplants the radical Western's apparatus-unmasking into gameplay.

game_elements.element: Lifelike-NPC behavior (NPCs work/chat/persist regardless of player in RDR vs. aimless GTA crowds)
game_elements.how_treated: 'World exists despite the player' (RDR) vs 'world exists for the player' (GTA); read as technical advance and as camouflage of player-centrality.

themes: Open-world freedom as designed/illusory; every choice already made
Games as procedural-rhetorical, ideology-bearing cultural artifacts; necessity of video-game literacy and critical analysis
The Western as a vehicle for left critique (Spaghetti Western -> AAA game); cultural borrowing, renegotiation, demonic satire of neoliberalism
Neoliberal 'end of history' (Zizek) vs. persistence of utopian hope
Reflexive gap between progressive game content and exploitative game-industry labor
Series-as-canon: ideology legible only across the whole arc
Designer-player power relation as simulated class struggle

Alexander Galloway (active vision; mutable game time/space)

Perez Latorre and Dyer-Witheford & de Peuter (GTA as neoliberal critique / 'game of Empire')

debate_axis_positions.position: Firmly critical-ideological pole; an explicit Althusserian ideology critique, not a celebratory/aesthetic appreciation.

Subversive-critique end. Against the dominant reading (RDR reproduces neoliberalism/exceptionalism/white-supremacy/hegemonic-masculinity), Tuominen argues the series unmasks and critiques the neoliberal state and is 'mainstream but radically progressive.'

debate_axis_positions.axis: framing tradition: American cultural artifact <-> European critique-of-capitalism tradition
debate_axis_positions.position: Shifts the debate toward situating RDR in the European (Spaghetti-Western) tradition of capitalism critique, against Humphreys/Bagnoli/Morgan who read it as an American artifact.
Series-as-whole; insists RDR2+RDR be read as one entity, which yields the progressive reading and distinguishes it from all cited single-title studies.
Holds both: praises progressive content while condemning Rockstar's exploitative production (the 'Rockstar contradiction'), preventing the progressive reading from sliding into studio endorsement.

tensions: Author reflexivity (reading may be 'mere opinions' shaped by his white North-European proletarian gamer position) vs. strong claims to well-grounded analysis
Progressive game content vs. Rockstar's exploitative crunch-culture production (the 'Rockstar contradiction')
Real mechanical player agency (honor, 'freedom') vs. fixed narrative outcomes and irrelevant in-game money (full interpellation)
Honor as moral system vs. honor's incoherence (must commit vice to act heroic; KKK-killing exempt)
Series-as-whole method (yields the thesis) vs. reduced comparability with single-title cluster studies (admitted re: Donald & Reid)
